newsitem.title: UK: Hearts slides in weak soccer sector.
newsitem.headline: Hearts slides in weak soccer sector.

text.p: Shares in newly-floated Scottish soccer club Heart of Midlothian Plc HTM.L dropped on Thursday, reflecting overall weakness in the sector, analysts said.
Hearts shares, issued at 140p on Monday, slid 11-1/2p to 118-1/2p by 1310 GMT.
"There is no support for these shares, they are in free-fall" said one dealer. "Even the shop (the company's broker) can't seem to find buyers," he said.
Guy Feld, analyst at securities house UBS, said shares in Hearts had been dragged lower by the lack of investor enthusiasm in the sector.
"Hearts is good little club run by sensible people but the sector is out of favour," said Feld.
"Look at Aston Villa. That's a recent issue and that's off 25 per cent since share dealings started."
Nick Batram, sports analyst at Greig Middleton & Co, said the sector was experiencing a bout of consolidation after the sharp gains earlier in the soccer season.
"The problem is the sector moved up too far, too quickly. Then some issues came to the market fully priced and this has hurt sentiment," said Batram.
Shares in Aston Villa Plc, issued earlier this month at 11.00 stg, fell 2-1/2p on Thursday to 822-1/2p, just above their all-time low of 820p.

Elsewhere in the sector, recently-relegated Sunderland Plc fell 2-1/2p to 427-1/2p and Southampton Leisure Plc, which narrowly avoided relegation from the Premier league this season, dropped one penny to 104p.
Sector leader Manchester United Plc was unchanged at 620p.
